Each internal node has `r` children, except possibly the last one, which takes whatever nodes are left. This is the shape of a binary heap (`r=2`), and it differs from the balanced tree (see `add_balanced_tree()`) in that you choose the number of nodes rather than the height, so the last level may be only partly filled. The root is the first node created. In a directed graph every edge points from parent to child. The tree is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Full r-ary trees are useful for: - modeling heaps and other array-backed trees, where a node's children sit at fixed positions - hierarchies with a fixed span of control but any total size (an org chart in which every manager has `r` reports) - test cases for tree algorithms with an exact node count ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Branching factor: the number of children of every full internal node. Must be at least `1`; `r=1` produces a path. [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes. Must be at least `1`. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; IDs run in breadth-first order, so the root is `"1"` in an empty graph. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `r=` or `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A binary tree of six nodes fills the first two levels and starts the third: ::: {#e993f2cc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_full_rary_tree(r=2, n=6) graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1->2', '1->3', '2->4', '2->5', '3->6'] ``` ::: ::: As in a heap, node `i`'s children are nodes `2i` and `2i + 1` (counting from `1`): ::: {#cf31e727 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_successors("2")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['4', '5'] ``` ::: :::
